title: 01. Foundations: GGUF — Complete Deep Dive
summary: GGUF (GPT-Generated Unified Format) is a binary file format that packages an entire LLM — weights, tokenizer, hyperparameters, and metadata — into a single portable file, with built-in quantization support.

sections.title: What Is GGUF?
sections.body: > **GGUF (GPT-Generated Unified Format) is a binary file format that packages an entire LLM — weights, tokenizer, hyperparameters, and metadata — into a single portable file, with built-in quantization support. It replaced the older GGML format in August 2023.**

sections.title: GGUF File Structure — Internals
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              GGUF FILE STRUCTURE (BINARY FORMAT)                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  A GGUF file is a binary file with this layout:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  MAGIC NUMBER (4 bytes): "GGUF"                         │
  │  Identifies this as a valid GGUF file                   │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │  VERSION (4 bytes): 1, 2, or 3                          │
  │  GGUF format version for compatibility                  │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │  TENSOR COUNT (8 bytes)                                 │
  │  How many weight tensors in this file                   │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │  METADATA KEY-VALUE COUNT (8 bytes)                     │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │  METADATA KEY-VALUE PAIRS                               │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
  │  general.architecture  = "llama"                        │
  │  general.name          = "LLaMA-3 8B Instruct"          │
  │  general.quantization_version = 2                       │
  │  general.file_type     = 15  (Q4_K_M)                   │
  │  llama.context_length  = 8192                           │
  │  llama.embedding_length= 4096                           │
  │  llama.block_count     = 32                             │
  │  llama.feed_forward_length = 14336                      │
  │  llama.attention.head_count = 32                        │
  │  llama.attention.head_count_kv = 8                      │
  │  llama.attention.layer_norm_rms_epsilon = 0.00001       │
  │  llama.rope.freq_base  = 500000.0                       │
  │  tokenizer.ggml.model  = "gpt2"                         │
  │  tokenizer.ggml.tokens = ["<|begin_of_text|>", ...]     │
  │  tokenizer.ggml.scores = [0.0, 0.0, ...]                │
  │  tokenizer.ggml.token_type = [3, 3, ...]                │
  │  tokenizer.chat_template = "{% if messages[0]... %}"    │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │  TENSOR INFO ARRAY                                      │
  │  For each tensor:                                       │
  │    name:   "blk.0.attn_q.weight"                        │
  │    n_dims: 2                                            │
  │    shape:  [4096, 4096]                                 │
  │    type:   Q4_K (quantization type)                     │
  │    offset: 0x0000A3F0 (byte offset in file)             │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │  ALIGNMENT PADDING                                      │
  │  Pad to 32-byte alignment for fast memory mapping       │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │  TENSOR DATA (bulk of file)                             │
  │  Raw quantized weight bytes for all tensors             │
  │  Memory-mapped at inference time (no copy needed!)      │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  WHY GGUF IS BETTER THAN SAFETENSORS FOR INFERENCE:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  safetensors (HuggingFace):          GGUF (llama.cpp):
  ──────────────────────────          ──────────────────────────
  Multiple files (model shards)       ONE single file
  Separate tokenizer files            Tokenizer INSIDE file
  Separate config.json                Config INSIDE file
  No built-in quantization            Built-in quantization
  Python/PyTorch required             C++ (no Python needed)
  FP16/BF16 only (16-bit min)         2-bit to 16-bit options
  Slower loading (copy to RAM)        Fast (memory-mapped)
  GPU focused                         CPU + GPU both supported

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  GGUF QUANTIZATION TYPES — DETAILED:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  TYPE      FILE_TYPE  BITS   DESCRIPTION
  ────────  ─────────  ────   ─────────────────────────────────
  F32       0          32     Full precision FP32
  F16       1          16     Half precision FP16
  Q4_0      2          4.5    4-bit, basic block quantization
  Q4_1      3          5.0    4-bit, with min/max per block
  Q5_0      6          5.5    5-bit, basic
  Q5_1      7          6.0    5-bit, with min/max
  Q8_0      8          8.5    8-bit, no zero point
  Q2_K      10         2.63   2-bit K-quant (mixed precision)
  Q3_K_S    11         3.0    3-bit K-quant small
  Q3_K_M    12         3.35   3-bit K-quant medium
  Q3_K_L    13         3.6    3-bit K-quant large
  Q4_K_S    14         4.0    4-bit K-quant small
  Q4_K_M    15         4.85   4-bit K-quant medium ← BEST DEFAULT
  Q5_K_S    16         5.0    5-bit K-quant small
  Q5_K_M    17         5.68   5-bit K-quant medium
  Q6_K      18         6.56   6-bit K-quant
  IQ2_XXS   28         2.06   imatrix 2-bit extra small
  IQ2_XS    29         2.31   imatrix 2-bit small
  IQ3_XXS   30         3.06   imatrix 3-bit extra small
  IQ4_XS    37         4.25   imatrix 4-bit extra small

  K-QUANT vs REGULAR:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Q4_0: ALL layers quantized to 4-bit uniformly
  Q4_K_M: Different layers get different precision:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Layer Type          Q4_K_M Precision                   │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │  token_embd          Q6_K (6-bit) — most critical       │
  │  output              Q6_K (6-bit) — final layer         │
  │  attention (qkv)     Q4_K (4-bit) — important           │
  │  attention (out)     Q4_K (4-bit)                       │
  │  feed_forward gate   Q4_K (4-bit)                       │
  │  feed_forward up     Q4_K (4-bit)                       │
  │  feed_forward down   Q6_K or Q4_K                       │
  │  layer_norm          F32 (full!) — tiny but critical     │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  Same average bit-width as Q4_0, MUCH better quality! ✅

  IMATRIX QUANTIZATION (newest, best quality):
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  IQ = Importance Matrix quantization.

  Regular K-quant: assigns bits by layer type (fixed rules)
  IQ: measures ACTUAL importance of each weight using
      calibration data → allocates bits where they matter most

  IQ4_XS vs Q4_K_M:
  Same size, IQ4_XS is measurably better quality.
  Why? It knows WHICH specific weights are critical,
       not just which layer types are critical.
```

sections.title: GGUF Naming Convention
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              READING GGUF FILENAMES                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  FORMAT:
  ModelName-Params-Variant-QuantType.gguf

  EXAMPLES:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf
  ─────────── ─── ──────── ───────
  Model name  Size Variant  Quant type

  Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2-Q5_K_M.gguf
  ─────────── ─── ──────── ──── ───────
  Model name  Size Variant  ver  Quant

  Llama-3.2-90B-Vision-Instruct-IQ2_XXS.gguf
  ──────── ─── ─────── ──────── ───────
  Model   size variant  task    Quant(tiny!)

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  CHOOSING THE RIGHT QUANT:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Available RAM    Recommended    Quality
  ─────────────    ───────────    ─────────────────────────
  2-3 GB          Q2_K           ⚠️ Degraded, emergency only
  4 GB            Q3_K_M         ▓▓▓░ Acceptable
  6 GB            Q4_K_M         ▓▓▓▓ Good ← most people
  8 GB            Q5_K_M         ▓▓▓▓▓ Very good
  10 GB           Q6_K           ▓▓▓▓▓▓ Excellent
  16+ GB          Q8_0 / F16     ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓ Near-perfect

  RULE: Use the largest quant that fits in your RAM
        with ~20% overhead for KV cache.
```
